aspect: The first obstacle is the counter
description: Reports are commonly discouraged as family matters, met with demands for money to open a case or fuel a vehicle, or handled by officers who tell the complainant to reconsider.
energy_note: Paying, to have a crime against you written down.

aspect: Medical evidence requires money and speed
description: A medical report requires a hospital, a fee, and attendance before the evidence degrades - all within hours, at the worst possible moment, usually without transport.
energy_note: Evidence with a deadline, and a fee, on the same night.

aspect: Settlement out of court is the default outcome
description: Family mediation, an apology, a payment, sometimes a marriage. The case ends without a record, which is why conviction figures are so low and why the low figures are then cited as evidence the offences are rare.
energy_note: Resolved, unrecorded, and then counted as not having happened.

aspect: The law exists and lives in a different building
description: VAPP 2015 expanded the definition of rape and criminalised harmful widowhood practices. Kano has not enacted it; implementation is uneven across states; and in August 2024 a bill to repeal it reached second reading in the Senate.
energy_note: A good law, unevenly adopted, and nearly repealed.
notes: See WOM-001 for the full legislative picture.

description: The officer asks whether she wants to 'spoil the man's life' and suggests she return in the morning with her uncle. She returns in the morning with her uncle. The matter is settled between the families by the following Sunday and no report is ever written.
